_comment: Public safety notices for the Today board. THE TRIGGER IS THE POLICE (or another responsible authority) ASKING FOR SOMETHING TO BE COMMUNICATED TO THE PUBLIC — not our own judgement that something sounds alarming. Without that rule this becomes a general alerts channel and every unresolved local crime turns into a candidate, which is exactly what the register's police policy exists to prevent. A notice must also be ACTIONABLE: what to look for, what to do, who to tell. 'Be vigilant' is noise and does not go up. ONE notice at a time, and never longer than 14 days — a permanent banner is wallpaper and stops being read. `expires` is the last day it shows, in Largs wall-clock time; the build drops it automatically after that, so there is nothing to remember to take down. The same matter stays in the Council corner register afterwards, because it happened and it is part of the record.
_rules: Only where the police or another responsible authority has asked for it to be communicated.
Only where a resident can act on it.
Never names an individual, a victim, a suspect, or an ongoing investigation.
Maximum 14 days. One at a time.
Sourced from a public record — normally the Community Council minutes — and linked to it.

notices.title: Counterfeit notes reported in Largs
notices.body: Counterfeit banknotes have been passed to businesses in the town. The notes feel slightly different to genuine ones, and the silver hologram strip can be peeled away. The Bank of England publishes a short guide to checking notes. If you are given one, report it to the police on 101.
notices.source: Raised with Police Scotland at the Community Council meeting of 16 April 2026, where it was agreed the problem should be communicated to residents.
